column1: # Applied symbol names for pulse-psp BOOT.BIN (image base 0x08804000).
# The evidence lives in the page named in the last column; this file exists so
# the names can be re-applied to a fresh Ghidra database without hand-editing.
# Run `just apply-names` after importing BOOT.BIN. See ADR-0005: the pages are
# the record of truth, and scripts/apply-ghidra-names.py checks that every row
# here still appears in its evidence page before it renames anything.
# kind is `function` or `data`. Confidence below 70 gets a `_q` suffix applied,
# below 50 is skipped. Recovered library and import symbols keep their real
# names rather than the project's Subsystem_VerbNoun scheme.
# Camera: the player-selectable in-race views and the on-disc parameter blocks.
# The generic XML reader: one scanning parser behind the front end, the handling
# stats and the camera blocks. Structurally identical to the PS2's.
# Import stubs are not listed here. They are derived from the binary's own NID
# tables by scripts/resolve-psp-imports.py, which verifies every name against
# the NID it must hash to; see imports.md.
